hypotheses.justification: `chartAlgFin` is the abbrev `chartAlg R F {j}` (Definitions/Def_AlgebraicCurve_TwoChartIntegralModel.lean:142) whose *type* is `Subalgebra R F`; the section variable `[Fact (j ≠ 0)]` that is in scope where it is defined occurs neither in that type nor in the elaborated value (`chartAlg R F {j}` uses only `R`, `F`, the ring/field/algebra instances and `j`), and Lean's section-variable pruning for non-theorem declarations (`Meta.removeUnused`, Lean/Meta/CollectFVars.lean:53) keeps exactly the section variables occurring in the type or value. Hence `chartAlgFin R F a` elaborates with no `Fact (a ≠ 0)` argument (the same is visible in the library, e.g. `omit [Fact (j ≠ 0)] [Fact (j' ≠ 0)] in` around statements using `chartAlgInf R F j`/`jInvChartInf R F j` in P2M/Sol/S_AlgebraicCurve_TwoChartIntegralModel_exists_iso_of_mem_chartAlgFin_of_forall_exists_mul_mem.lean:17), so the statement still elaborates after deleting the binder. The proof does not use the fact either: the monotonicity lemma `chartAlgFin_le_of_mem` (lines 77–94 of this file) never mentions its `[Fact (a ≠ 0)] [Fact (b ≠ 0)]` binders — the argument is only `Algebra.adjoin_le (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hab)`, `IsIntegral.map_of_comp_eq` and `isIntegral_trans` — so a Fact-free copy of it gives `chartAlgFin R F a ≤ chartAlgFin R F b`, and symmetrically `≥`, whence `le_antisymm`. The degenerate case `a = 0` is covered because that ≤-proof is uniform in `a`: `0 ∈ chartAlgFin R F b` holds for any `b` (it is a subalgebra), and `chartAlgFin R F 0` is just `integralClosure R F`, so no non-vanishing is needed. The same binder `[Fact (b ≠ 0)]` can be deleted at the same time, using the same Fact-free version of `chartAlgFin_le_of_mem` in both directions.

Identical argument with the roles of `a` and `b` exchanged. `chartAlgFin R F b` (`chartAlg R F {b}`, type `Subalgebra R F`) takes no `Fact (b ≠ 0)` argument, so the conclusion `chartAlgFin R F a = chartAlgFin R F b` still elaborates without the binder, and the proof of `chartAlgFin_le_of_mem` (lines 77–94) uses only `hab : a ∈ chartAlgFin R F b`, `Algebra.adjoin_le`, `IsIntegral.map_of_comp_eq` and `isIntegral_trans`, never the `Fact` instances. A Fact-free version of that lemma applied to `hab` and `hba` plus `le_antisymm` proves the statement in full generality, including the case `b = 0` (where `chartAlgFin R F 0 = integralClosure R F` and `0 ∈ chartAlgFin R F a` is automatic). This binder and `[Fact (a ≠ 0)]` may be removed simultaneously.
